utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If I could remind you of the affirmation which still applies. Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness Hutsch. Can we continue?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You recall that yesterday we ended when I showed you a photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: For which you claimed it was a vehicle of the Zastava type, while I claimed that this was a vehicle of the Golf type. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown P12.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember this photograph? Do you remember having been shown this photograph yesterday and that this was the vehicle that you saw in the courtyard of Elmaz Jusufi on the 14th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you testified that this was a vehicle of the type Zastava. Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This was on yesterday's transcript, the unofficial transcript, on the last page, page 91 of yesterday's transcript, where you say: [In English] "At the moment all, I can say is that -- is that it was a Golf. "Can you claim that this is a vehicle of the Zastava brand? Is that correct?" [Interpretation] And your answer was "Yes." Do you recall this? This is line 13 and 14 of yesterday's transcript, of the official page 6424. Do you recall that yesterday you confirmed that this was a vehicle of the Zastava type?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where -- where did you ask me if it was a Zastava? Where is that there on the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I put it to that you this is what your answer was as in yesterday's transcript. Once again, I will repeat, this is 19 -- 13th line on the 91st page, when I showed you this photograph which is also evidence 1D2, and I asked you: [In English] "This is a vehicle of the Zastava brand. Is that correct?" [Interpretation] And then you answered in the affirmative, and you said "Yes." Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are showing to me now, as to whether that is a Zastava, what I'm reading here, I said, "No, that is true." But you never asked me whether there was a Zastava there, that it was insinuated. You seem to be getting new directions from someone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask the witness not to make comments about counsel. I would be grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I see no reason to make any comment at the moment. Carry on, Mr. Apostolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to say to you when -- when the witness Elmaz Jusufi was shown this evidence, P12, he responded that: "This photograph shows the courtyard, the entrance courtyard -- gate to the courtyard, and the vehicle Golf II which was registered in my name." Can you agree with me that this is a vehicle of the Golf type?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it is very likely. I'm not a expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you agree that the witness spoke the truth about his own vehicle?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason to doubt that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now please be shown P320, page 2. One page further down. The English version is yet another page further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see on the screen before you? Do you see the notes you have made for the 14th?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see where it is written: [In English] "[Previous translation continues] ... reportedly put petrol on the car, Zastava, and set fire to it." [Interpretation] Do you see this on the screen?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this your official note?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is a note.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you have noted that in question was a vehicle of the Zastava make?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You're taking this out of context without discussing the details with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I would like to ask you: Did you note down that the vehicle in question was a Zastava?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I made myself a note as to whether it was a Zastava because the person I was talking to talked about his car but didn't mention the model, and I don't have any great idea about cars. I'm not have interested in cars, and I just made a note here and I see -- you can see it is in brackets. The things that are in brackets are things that have to be checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Why is a Zastava put down then?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I made a note about it here as to whether it was a Zastava, but I was not sure and did not know whether it was a Zastava. I think we discussed this yesterday. You asked me yesterday whether I could recognise a Golf I to VI, and I said "no."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You wish then to say, because this was put in parenthesis, that this would not be correct. This would not be correct. Is that what you want to say?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a working note, and we discussed yesterday that none of these interviews, none of the information from third parties had been verified.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: But you saw this vehicle with your own eyes. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And then you wrote down "Zastava." Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote it to help me remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just answered your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the answer is "yes."

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote "Zastava" there. Yes, that's my writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that your testimony before this Court is based on your notes?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Does this mean that the other information from your notes are also incorrect?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to explain to you, these are notes to serve to help my memory; and, at the very start, I tried to explain to you that at the end of each day we went and wrote down what we had observed that day, to try to verify things. I explained to Mr. Mettraux that the whole Ljuboten issue, problem did not give rise to any further need for investigation because a lot of issues would have to have been verified and properly investigated in order to report on them neutrally and objectively, and that's what you're doing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, our case is that you were never in Ljuboten on the 12th and 14th of August, 2001. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll have to quote Saint Augustine once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You don't have to quote him now. Just answer the question.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is that that is wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for your answer. I will now continue. On Saturday, the 11th of August, you were in Ljubanci. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: In Ljubanci, you went with your white Jeep, Land Rover. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your interpreter was with you, a Macedonian. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You went by the road from Radisani towards Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether there was a check-point of the Macedonian security forces before the village of Ljubanci on the 11th of August, 2001?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you tell me from your conversations with others what you mean by "check-point"?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: By this, I mean a place where control is conducted by the security forces of vehicles and persons which enter the village. There are sandbags, trenches.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. The army of the Republic of Macedonia had a control centre at the school at the village of Ljubanci, is this correct, the army of the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What -- what do you mean by "control centre"?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is what you have stated. You have called it a control point in -- command post. Command post, this is what you said in your notes. Do you agree that you have said that the ARM had a command centre in village of Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Then you agree with me that this is correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: A logistics centre of the army of the Republic of Macedonia in the village of Ljubanci was in the children's rest house. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of unconfirmed information, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you now testifying before this Court that the logistics centre of the ARM was at the children's rest house. Is this correct? "Yes" or "no," please?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Thank you. You arrived in Ljubanci in 9.00 a.m. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you say so. I'd have to verify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: When you entered the village of Ljubanci on the 11th of August, 2001, can you tell us where you parked your Jeep?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the entrance to the village. When you enter, it would be on the right side in a street, on a street that leads to the road that goes to Ljuboten on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Afterwards, you moved on foot through the village. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You arrived to the school where the command point -- post of the army of the Republic of Macedonia was located?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you describe to me the school where the command post was located, the number of floors, whether it was one building, two buildings, three buildings, whether there was a fence, whether there was a courtyard?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a school courtyard. If I remember rightly, it had a yellow wall with a rust-colour iron fence, I would say. On the left was the main building, which had several storeys. It was in a L-shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown 65 ter 2D401.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is probably the school, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we seek to tender this document into evidence because the witness confirmed that this was the school in the village of Ljubanci where the -- where the centre was located.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just as a matter of relevance, can we ask whether this photograph depicts the school today or as it was in 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not the school in Ljubanci at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, then, I would object to it's being tendered into evidence, Your Honour. There's no relevance then to this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The relevance pertains to the credibility of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have shown the witness a photograph. He said it was "probably," I think, was his word, the school, and now you say that it is not the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I showed a photograph to the witness, and I asked him what he sees on this photograph and whether he recognises it, and he responded that this is perhaps the school --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Probably the school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, the record, for what it's worth, Mr. Apostolski, shows that on your account the witness has identified a photograph as being probably of the school he's describing, which you say is not the school. Now, how do we see the photograph itself as relevant? The record shows that he was shown a photograph. He says it is probably the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, in line with the previous questioning, I was asking him about the school in the village of Ljubanci where the witness even previously was describing the school in this village of Ljubanci; therefore, in question here is that particular school. My question was about that particular school.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, at the moment, we could go as far as marking it for identification, Mr. Apostolski, in case there's going to be some evidence about it, but I don't see that we can take it any further than that. It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D72, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that on Sunday, 12th of August, 2001, between 7.15 and 8.15 [as interpreted], you arrived at the control check-point in Radisani. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that you didn't know that there was a bus terminal over there?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And from there, you were observing what is going on in the village of Ljuboten at 8.00 in the morning on the 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the bus terminal?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: No, from the place where the check-point in Radisani was located.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you could tell me again what you define as being a "check-point."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: You said that on Sunday, 12th of August, between 7.15 and 7.30 [as interpreted], you arrived at the check-point in Radisani. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to avoid a misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... according to your understanding, this would a qualify as a control -- check-point?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And from this check-point, you observed what is going on in the village of Ljuboten at 8.00 in the morning on the 12th of August, 2001.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please tell me what was your observation point?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my best -- the best of my knowledge, it was in a photograph and also in a spot on a map that I marked out.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, but can you tell me how far this location was from the check-point, of the check-point Radisani?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you any precise answer to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was this on the road towards Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was this on the road towards Skopje?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Which road did you follow after the check-point in Radisani?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the direction of Ljubanci.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I just asked you that. I asked you a while ago whether from the check-point Radisani, in the direction towards Ljubanci, whether this was the location of your initial observation point, and you answered "no." Can you please tell me what is correct then?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me whether my observation point was on the road to Ljubanci, and that was not the case; under 39:54.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: I'm asking you whether your observation point was on the road.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please tell me where it was?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I marked it clearly in the photograph and also on the map, as far as I could identify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown evidence P307 -- Exhibit P307, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you see the photograph in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is this the location that you used for your -- as an observation point? Does this photograph that is shown in front of you give the same view as from your observation point?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as the first part of the question is concerned, mine was slightly further back; and the second part of the question, yes, the reply is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please describe and tell us how many metres further back was your observation point?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Looking at this photograph, I cannot tell you, at least not precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please tell me in metres.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Describe what was there in the immediate neighbourhood, whether there was a forest or anything else?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a row of trees. I'm not a biologist. It could have been a apple tree, but I'm really not quite sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was there a plowed land around?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Plowed land is as a field, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was there a field that was cultivated that would have some types of crops?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are "crops"?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So any type of agricultural products or wheat that is being seed placed in the land. So was this an agricultural land?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was a land cultivated by farmers around, but I cannot tell you what type of fields they were; and, secondly, I can tell you what -- which kind of plant was cultivated there, and I cannot give you the exact distance between that and the tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: During your testimony, you said that this hill in front of you, number 631, was a obstacle; and, in order to observe better, then you moved to a second observation point. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: On this photograph, can you please mark with an "X" the location where you moved, where the second observation point was? Can you indicate this with a arrow, please, in which direction would that be.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's already been marked with the arrow number "1," but I would like to point out this was just the very rough location, not exact location; and, certainly, it wouldn't describe exactly in metres where our location was.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please mark with an "X" your second observation point, the location of it?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you want me to mark it precisely?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: As precise as you can be.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Having said that this is just a very rough location. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Thank you. Can you please tell me how did you arrive from the first observation point to the second observation point?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Via land that was being used by farmers --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Paths, paths.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you go on foot?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went by vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, can you draw this path that you were following on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I'm in a position to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Were you moving along a asphalt road to this particular location?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So from the position "1" to the position number "2," you were moving exclusively along a dirt road. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already stated, it was a path that was being used by farmers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So that the transcript is not confusing, Mr. Apostolski, he moved from position "1" to a position marked with an "X," not position "2." "2" is a different location.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, that is correct. I used the number "2" because he was talking about a couple of observation points. So, we are describing position or observation point "2," which is marked with an "X" on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please confirm that when you were moving towards the position marked with an "X," you were moving along a dirt road or a path?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And you were not walking on foot. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we would like to tender this photograph with this additional "X" as -- into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D73, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, you claim that there was a dirt path or track between these two observation points. Is this what you testify before this Court?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated that there were paths which were being used by farmers.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you please answer only with "yes" or "no." Is it correct that, from your first observation point to the second observation point that you marked with an "X" on the photograph, there was a dirt road? Can you please answer this question with "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And with your vehicle, you managed to go from the first to the second observation point in a period of 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. You said that, as of September 2001, you have been working at the German embassy. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Your superior was Mr. Peter Matthiesen.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I am able to talk about this in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No restrictions have been placed on that, so you can.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you discuss with him and did you exchange information with him regarding the security situation in the Republic of Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know that there were a couple of German soldiers who were sent to observe the events on the 10th and 11th of August in the villages of Ljuboten and Ljubanci?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that they did not manage to enter either the first or the second village? They did not manage to enter the village of Ljuboten on the 10th and the 11th of August.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And the reason for this were the police check-points which surrounded the village of Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as this detail is concerned, we would have to talk about it in closed session.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't see any reasons why we should move to a private session and discuss this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you discuss with Mr. Matthiesen this situation regarding Ljuboten, the fact that the German soldiers were not able to enter the village?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't talk about it with Mr. Matthiesen but with the person concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: And did you talk about anything in relation to Ljuboten with Mr. Matthiesen?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: So the German soldiers were not able to enter Ljuboten on Friday and Saturday before the action because of the police check-points, and you managed to do so during the action on the 12th of August to walk to the village of Ljuboten and to have a chat with Mr. Johan Tarculovski and Goran Stojkov who, later on, most kindly, have seen you off?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reasons as to why the German soldiers -- you are saying, you're implying that we're talking about soldiers in a military vehicle and in uniform. So as far as the soldiers are concerned, this is slightly different in the report that they wrote, but I cannot talk about it any further in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Why do you say that, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because staff, as well as the circumstances, involve security interests of the Federal Republic of Germany.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: But they have not placed any such restriction on you giving evidence relevant to this case, you see. You're trying to impose a condition which the German government has not imposed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the case is this: The information concerned my time during -- concerned my time at the German embassy and the information that I obtained while I was there, and we noted yesterday that one of the people concerned had refused to give testimony to this Tribunal. I would have to look into the circumstances closely to which I was subjected during my time as an aide to the military attache.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're being asked, Mr. Hutsch, about events in August when you were not an attache.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is being put to me as to why these two soldiers could not get into Ljuboten. I know the statement made by the soldiers and I know their report, which I heard about in September or October, and then I was a member of the embassy; otherwise, I could only speculate which might not be keeping in the truth and not answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know several people called "Hoxha."

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: This is Samedin Xhezairi?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: He was your liaison with the NLA. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What do you mean by "my liaison with the NLA"?

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Was he your connection, your liaison with the NLA?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 2D54.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you see the photograph on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you recognise the person marked with the number "1"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that the person in question is Samedin Xhezairi, Hoxha?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you receive information from him about the NLA?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did you ever receive information from this person?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Do you know the person marked with "5"?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Can you tell us who this person is?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's Ali Ahmeti.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Can you tell us that the person, Samedin Xhezairi, had links with Al Qaeda, with the terrorist organisation Al Qaeda?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the result of research that I carried out in 2004, and was the subject of a program on ZDF, the second German television station, in November 2004, about which I was criticised by Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Did this person have connections with the terrorist organisation -- group Al Qaeda?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a result of my research, I would say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Do you not know whether Ali Ahmeti, Gezim Ostreni maintained connection with Al Qaeda through this person?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to speculate to answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Therefore, you cannot give me a answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I could give you more information about the period when I was on the staff of the military attache, but we would have to return to closed session to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: No, thank you. This was my only question and you answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness please be shown photograph 65 ter 2D397.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember rightly, this is at the edge of Ljubanci, and the street on the right goes towards Ljuboten and the street on the left, where the red car is standing, is probably the road to -- from the rest house in Ljuboten.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to -- to mark this photograph for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 2D74, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Witness, the case of the Defence is that you have never met Mr. Tarculovski, neither in Tetovo nor in Ljuboten. You could not have seen him in Tetovo because in 2001 Tarculovski was never in Tetovo, neither privately nor on official business. When there was official travel with Ohrid, together with the family of President Trajkovski, due to security reason it was forbidden to go along the highway Skopje-Tetovo-Gostivar-Kicevo-Ohrid, and this was done by helicopter, or by Bitola-Prilep-Ohrid. In the front line, Johan was only in the Kumanovo area, as the security of the president, of President Trajkovski, only on one occasion and for only several hours. Do you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: You would be forcing me to draw a conclusion that I would not like to draw.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Is it correct that you have never seen Mr. Tarculovski neither in Tetovo nor in Ljuboten. This is the case of the Defence. Is this correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. APOSTOLSKI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Apostolski. Is that probably a convenient time, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Probably, it would make more sense to take the first break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume then at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, you were asked during your cross-examination about a lawsuit that you were engaged with in Germany with respect to an article that had been written by a man, I believe, named Mr. Rub. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness 65 ter 1D370, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Help us, Mr. Hutsch. Can you clarify for us why this article was printed in the Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: The district court and the higher district court in Hamburg gave two separate decisions stipulating that the article by Mr. Rub was based on insufficient research; and, in order not to drag out proceedings for another three years with damages, the presiding judge of the district court convinced both parties involved to reach a compromise in the matter. This article was one element of the compromise achieved, and it was designed to rehabilitate me and to show that the claims of Colleague Rub were not properly researched, both in my case and in the reporting on the so-called massacre in Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can I just ask you one more thing. When I use the term "compromise" here, you're referring to agreement between the parties?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that this document be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I believe it is Exhibit 1D245, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I checked, and I did not see that. I'm very sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You were also asked earlier in your cross-examination -- actually, this was back in June at page 2853 and beyond in the transcript. My colleague Mr. Mettraux asked if any other -- well, he asked you some question about the interview that you had done with Ratko Mladic back in late 1995. My colleague asked you if any other journalist had interviewed Ratko Mladic after his indictment or if you knew of any other journalist. I'd like to play a video for you, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is a video-clip from Greek TV MEGA, made in the city of Pale, Republika Srpska, on the 4th of March, 1996, if we can watch this, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, did you recognise the gentleman with grey hair and dressed in camouflage colour shown in the video requesting questions?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There is no doubt about it, that was Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, if Ratko Mladic was indicted in July of 2005 [sic] and this interview occurred in March of 2006 [sic], at least this journalist asking questions here managed to reach and interview Mr. Mladic after he was indicted. Would that be fair?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was actually no problem until December 1996 to get a interview with Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this video-clip, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, simply to query the relevance of this. We haven't seen the evidence of the date of the interview. We'll take Mr. Saxon' word for it, but the question, in this matter, was whether the witness in this case had had that interview. If Mr. Saxon now has found evidence that there was a interview after the indictment, the Defence would stand corrected on this, and we will take Mr. Saxon word as to the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Shall I respond, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, when Mr. Mettraux was cross-examining Mr. Hutsch in June about whether he had interviewed Mr. Mladic or not, one of the questions which he put to Mr. Hutsch, in fact more than once, was: Do you know of any other journalist who managed to interview Ratko Mladic after he was indicted? This was clearly insinuating that this was not possible to do, and that is the relevance of this clarification on re-direct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I mention first that, before it is lost from the screen, dates are shown, at lines 14 and 15 of page 28, as "2005" and "2006." I think they should be "1995" and "1996," respectfully. There can be no question about the relevance of your re-examination on this topic and the answers that you have received. What is the actual television record of the interview going to achieve? The transcript discloses that there was a television interview in this state which now accepted with the man in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Point taken, Your Honour. Very well. I will withdraw my request to tender this video.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to another.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, perhaps, before I move on to, simply to clarify the record as well, the Office of the Prosecutor received this video from the English news service ITN, from their archives of video-clips or from videos, and it was ITN which informed us of the date of the interview, March the 4th, 1996, in terms of their records.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, at page 6161 of the transcript, my colleague

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX SUGGESTED THAT
utterances.text: "But for a few additions or exaggerations, you took the information contained in your reporter's notes from 12 August 2001 [sic] almost verbatim from the report of Human Rights Watch that was published subsequently about the events in Ljuboten." And, later, on page 6169, my colleague suggested to you that you fabricated the information in your notes based on the report of Human Rights Watch. And, finally, on page 6171, my colleague suggested that: "All you did was lift information from the Human Rights Watch report, except for the odd few little changes which you inserted in it." Do you remember this discussion?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we show the witness, please, what is Exhibit P320. I apologise. I should have said reporter's notes from "14 August," not "12 August."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see, this is the first page of your notes from the 14th of August, Mr. Hutsch, and it shows the first person you spoke to in Ljuboten was Mr. Elmaz Jusufi. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you were speaking to him or he was giving you information about the death of his son Rami. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page, please, in both versions, and, perhaps, if we could focus on the top ten lines or so of text, please. No, we need to move up. I need to look at the top of the page. There we are. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Hutsch, the third entry there says: "MUP then reportedly poured petrol on the car (Zastava), and set fire to it." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So that is the information that you noted down about the burning of the car. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could I ask the court officer's assistance please. Can we now see Exhibit P352. This is the report published by Human Rights Watch. It was drafted by Mr. Peter Bouckaert. Can we turn, please, to page 7 in the English version, and -- what has ERN U000-0105 in the Macedonian version. I'm sorry. In the English version, it -- can we turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: If we can assist, Your Honour, we believe this would be U000-0106.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Actually, no, I think I'm looking for what I see in front of me right now; though, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You see, at the top of this page, Mr. Hutsch, Mr. Bouckaert is describing information that he received from Mr. Elmaz Jusufi. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And there are several paragraphs where he appears to quote Mr. Jusufi. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Could you please direct your attention to the third quoted paragraph. It begins with the phrase: "My car." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that sentence says this: "My car was parked in the front yard, right next to the gate. They poured gasoline on it and set it on fire. I heard the police say, 'Pour the gasoline.'" Do you see what I've read to you?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Would it be fair to say that there are details of information provided by Elmaz Jusufi to Human Rights Watch, their representative, which are included in the Human Rights Watch report about Ljuboten that are not in your notes of the 14th of August?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And if I may add, that such a direct quote for me, as a reporter, was worth its weight in gold, because it makes the story much more lively.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: In other words, are you saying that if you had received such a direct lively quote, you would have noted it down?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On page 6172 of the transcript, my colleague mentioned the ages of certain persons that are reflected in your reporter's notes of the 14th of August, and he asked you the following: "Isn't it correct, Mr. Hutsch, that the only persons whose age you mentioned in your notes are those which are mentioned in the Human Rights Watch report?" And you responded: "No," that you recorded the ages of persons who were interesting for you at the beginning of a investigation. Do you recall that exchange?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, let's just suppose for a moment, please. Let's suppose that someone did what Mr. Mettraux suggested that you did. Suppose someone lifted information from the Human Rights Watch report in order to create so-called reporter notes about interviews from persons from Ljuboten. Let's just imagine that for a moment, and let's suppose that the same person, as part of his or her lifting, if I can use that expression, of information from the Human Rights Watch also lifted information regarding ages of persons interviewed and placed the information about ages in their so-called reporter's notes. Let just suppose that scenario for a moment. Mr. Hutsch, logically, in that situation, would we expect to find that the ages of the persons mentioned in the supposedly fabricated reporter's notes are the same as the ages mentioned in the Human Rights Watch report?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we continue, please, with the Exhibit P352, the Human Rights Watch that is before us, and can we go to what is, I believe, page 9 in the English version and page U000-U107 in the Macedonian version. Perhaps, if I could ask Ms. Guduric's assistance, if we can zoom in on the last two paragraphs, please, in the English. Well, maybe we can -- I can't quite read the paragraph because of the margin. Is there any way that the second-to-last paragraph can be shown slightly smaller? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The second-to-the last paragraph reflects information received from Aziz Bajrami, and you see a line beginning, Mr. Hutsch: "Aziz Bajrami and his sons." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then the third sentence of that paragraph, we see this sentence: "The police officers then ordered Aziz Bajrami and another elderly man, 68-year-old Muharem Bajrami, to leave the scene." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we turn to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you see the paragraph, Mr. Hutsch, beginning with: "Two of the bodies." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Take a look, please, at the second sentence in that paragraph. It says this: "The two bodies were identified by villagers as Sulejman Bajrami, age 21, and Muharem Ramadani," which would have been really the person mentioned on the previous page, "aged 68." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we return now, please, to what is Exhibit P320, the notes -- Mr. Hutsch's reporter's notes of the 14th of August. And if we can turn, please, to what is the third page in the English version, and can we zoom in a bit on the top of that. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The first line that you wrote at the top of that page, it says: "Together with Muharem Bajrami (65)." Do you see that, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And that number "65," was that a indication of the gentleman's age?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So your notes, then, with respect to this gentleman, provide a different age than the Human Rights Watch report.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to move on to a different topic, Mr. Hutsch. Just a brief question or two about how you reported your stories. At page 6871 of the transcript, my colleague Mr. Mettraux asked you whether to have an article published in your newspaper in Hamburg on the next day, you would need to send the article by 8.00 the previous evening, and you replied: "In general, yes." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were there exceptions to the general 8.00 p.m. rule?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you explain, please, what kinds of circumstances would cause exceptions?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, when I was held up, then we got an extended deadline. Sometimes, I had to write several articles at once. For example, about one story I needed to write explanatory stores or I had to write a comment; then, the so-called boss, who was in charge, he then would tell me in which order I should send the articles, so that you could attach the pages; and then the editor or the deputy editor would -- he would then revise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just so that the record is clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry to intervene, Your Honour. But so that the record reflects accurately what was asked, Mr. Saxon has cited correctly, I believe, one part of the transcript. However, at page 2837 and 2838, the question was asked in the following term: "And what would the latest time so that it could be published in the next day issue?" The answer Mr. Hutsch was, and I quote: "The most latest time was 8.00 in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: That's true. That was from a earlier exchange between Mr. Hutsch and Mr. Mettraux from back in June.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You mentioned, Mr. Hutsch, you said: "For example, when I was held up, then we got an extended deadline." Just so the record is clear, what do you mean by "when I was held up"? What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be the situation, for example, when I was held up by checks, by controls, by cars breaking down, and, if I was then not in a position by a mobile telephone, to then send off my text. It happened on varies occasions, for example, on the road between Skopje and Tetovo where there was no reception for the mobile phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, when you use the phrase "held up," you mean or one definition of held up is when you were delayed.

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to discuss with you, Mr. Hutsch, a bit, the issue of machine-guns on armoured personnel carries. On Wednesday, between pages 6290 and 6303, there was a fairly long discussion between Mr. Mettraux and yourself about machine-guns and whether machine-guns were mounted on APCs used by the Ministry of Interior during the crisis in 2001. Do you recall that exchange?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And, at pages 6294 to 6295, my colleague showed you the statement of a Defence witness, Ms. Nikoletka Mitanova, and the following -- one of the sentences in that statement said: "After the crisis ended in November 2002, machine-guns were mounted on some of them," referring to APCs. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, you had a military career before you were a journalist, a war correspondent. From a military perspective, would it be logical to mount machine guns on APCs after a conflict ends?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that doesn't make any sense at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show what was marked for identification as Exhibit 1D239, please. Your Honour, these are the photos that Mr. Hutsch provided to the Chamber, I believe it was two days ago. I'm not 100 percent sure. Can we look at the next photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You'll recall, Mr. Hutsch, this was one of the photographs that you provided to the Chamber a couple of days ago, right?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And can you just briefly describe what are we seeing in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photo was taken in March/early April in Tetovo and -- no, that's not correct. In the western area of the barracks exactly opposite of the football stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, I appreciate that information, but can you please just tell me what do we see in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is an armoured personnel carrier BTR, which is firing towards the left, I think with a 14.5-millimetre machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we please show a photograph from Prosecution 65 ter number 202. This comes from a range N004-5235 to 5250, and it's page 16 within that range. Can we -- well, can we move backward one page, please. Okay. Can we move forward two pages, please. Can we move forward again, please. Can we look at perhaps what is N004-5250. That might simplify matters. My apologies, Your Honour. We're looking for a --

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: Do you have a copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Can I show you, Mr. Usher?

utterances.speaker: THE USHER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I need to show you the right photograph. This is the one we are looking for now, and then we look at these that follow it. That is certainly one of the photographs I would like to show. Can we go to the page before this, please. Well, I can work with this photograph here actually, if Ms. Guduric could assist me by focussing on the photograph of the man sitting in a turret with a helmet, please. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: For now, let's just look at this photograph, Mr. Hutsch. This comes from Reuters. It's dated the 3rd of May, 2001. The headline is: "A Macedonian policeman sits on top of an APC near Kumanovo." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And then, below that, there is a description, a short paragraph: "A Macedonian policeman in full combat gear sits on top of an APC on the road near the town of Kumanovo some 35 kilometres east from the capital Skopje on May the 3rd, 2001." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you see what appears to be a weapon in front of this Macedonian policeman?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is a machine-gun, 7.62-millimetres, and a Russian build.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Perhaps, if I could ask the usher's assistance again, and if to could pass there to Ms. Guduric. I see Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Simply, again, for the accuracy of the transcript again, Your Honour will remember that this particular picture, I believe, was admitted, however not the text of it, for obvious reasons, of reliability. The other matter which perhaps Mr. Saxon should clarify is whether the suggestion is being made in relation to the first picture that narrow was shown to Mr. Hutsch in this series - that was the picture of a green armoured vehicle - and whether it is the position of the Prosecution that this in fact a military or a police vehicle. Mr. Hutsch has indicated in his statement, and I believe also in his evidence, that the vehicles which he claims to have seen were blue in colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was not aware that this particular photograph had been admitted. That's the first point. The second point is, I was actually --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: As far as I know, it is not presently an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the first photograph that I showed Mr. Hutsch, I believe is in this series of news articles. That's why I was going through it, and I thought I had them pinpointed in series on a series of pages. I was going to show the witness the description of this scene as reflected in the news media. Perhaps I could assist, or Ms. Guduric, if she could take a look for this particular item, please. They're the same photographs, which I thought was on page 16 of this ERN range. [Trial Chamber confers].

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will finish today, Your Honour. I guarantee that I will finish today, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Even if it's midnight, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will finish, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I don't want to mislead Mr. Saxon. We are now checking to make sure this is it indeed the right picture or whether it was another picture from the same series. So we are attempting now to ascertain that fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, and I'm grateful to the Court Officers for their hard work and patience with me. After I run through this series of photographs, I will simply ask that they be admitted together as one exhibit, if that is possible, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, please take a look at the photograph at the top of this page here, over the headline, "Armed Macedonian policemen take aim in Tetovo." Do you see that photo?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Have you seen that photo recently?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is that the photo that I showed you a few manipulates ago, one of the photos that you provided to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Under the headline, it says: "19 March 2001, Reuters pictures," and then it says: "An armed Macedonian policeman takes aim with his sniper rifle in Tetovo some 50 kilometres south-west of the capital Skopje, March 19, 2001. Macedonian tanks enter Tetovo on Monday as police machine-gunned and mortared ethnic Albanian guerrilla positions on the sixth day of violence that has fueled fears of a new Balkan war." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: My concern, Mr. Saxon, is whether that caption which you read relates to the photograph above or the one below. I think you may need to turn to the bottom of the preceding page.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we do that, please. I stand corrected, Your Honour. Thank you very much for catching that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The headline over this paragraph says: "Armed Macedonian policeman shooting from his position in Tetovo." Again, it is dated the 19th of March, 2001, and, again, we see text: "An armed Macedonian policeman aims his sniper rifle as he and the armoured personnel carrier, which he is sheltering behind, fire on ethnic Albanian guerrilla positions in Tetovo," and, again, the same language about: "Macedonian tanks entered Tetovo on Monday as police machine-gunned and mortared ethnic Albanian guerrilla positions."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we now go to the next page, please, just the very next page, and at the top of the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, again, just for the record, Mr. Hutsch, that photograph, at the very top of N004-5244, that's one of the photographs that you provided to the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this particular news item with this photograph from the 19th of March, as well as the previous news item, which I believe was from May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: 3rd of May. Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We believe that the position should be similar to a previous occasion, where only the pictures have been admitted rather than the text. There's no evidence of the reliability of any of the content of the caption, as I think Mr. Saxon called it, which refer to the particular picture. More importantly, we believe, Your Honour, there is no indication whatsoever of the issue which matters in this particular incident, which is whether or not the vehicle in question was an army vehicle or a police vehicle. The evidence which was put to Mr. Hutsch during his evidence in chief was about the MOI having such vehicle. What the first picture showed, and that's the picture that Mr. Hutsch provided, is that this was a green vehicle in his evidence; and, in his statement, Mr. Hutsch said, "These APCs were in typical blue colour." That's his evidence. So, in the submissions of the Defence, the first picture that Mr. Saxon showed does not assist in any way the Prosecution case. The position of the Defence is that the pictures may provide some assistance to the Chamber, to the extent that it would show the presence of such a vehicle at the time in Tetovo. But we believe that the text has not been shown to be reliable, nor has any of the documents shown in any way that the vehicle in question were police vehicles, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, certainly, with respect to the photograph and text from the 3rd of May, we are told that that is a Macedonian policeman sitting on top of an APC. The witness has indicated that there was a machine gun in front of that policeman on top of that APC. Now, the witness may not be able to say that he was there and saw that particular policeman; But, in my mind, Your Honour, this is a matter of what weight to be given to the evidence, not a question of admissibility. Certainly, newspaper reports have been admitted in this trial previously. There's no bar to that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber will receive both photographs and the news captions, they being from a leading news agency; but it receives them subject to the question of the weight to be attached to them, this being clearly a second-hand report.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I can -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: They will be received as exhibit P483, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If I can receive from Ms. Guduric the package of papers that I passed to her, please. Mr. Usher, I may need your assistance in one moment, and perhaps Ms. Guduric could help me find this particular photograph and the caption above it. Yes. Thank you very much. This is it. Actually, could we go to up to the page above it, please, the bottom -- no, the page above it, please. The page before this, I'm sorry, and if you come to the top of this page, please. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of this page, we see the following headline: "A Macedonian policeman on a APC near Skopje." It is dated the 12th of August, 2001, and the description says this: "A Macedonian policeman watches from a APC on the road from Skopje to the northern village of Radusa, where five policemen were injured on August 11th, 2001. Macedonia accused ethnic Albanian guerrillas from neighbouring Kosovo of mounting attacks on Saturday, even as ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And if we can go to the next page, please, and if we can see the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: "... even as government and a local guerrilla leader expressed support for a plan meant plenty to avert a new Balkan war." Do you see the photograph there, Mr. Hutsch?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: There appears to be a weapon in front of the man in that turret. Can you tell anything about that weapon?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, again, that it is a machine-gun, 7.62 millimetres, Russian built.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would seek to tender this particular photograph and the description, and I would note that several witnesses have talked about the fighting in Radusa involving members of the Macedonian police during the weekend of the 10th to 12th of August, including Risto Galevski and Zoran Jovanovski and the involvement of police forces in that fighting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The photograph and caption will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P484, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please play for Mr. Hutsch Exhibit P453.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is a video, Mr. Hutsch, from July or August 2001.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we stop there. Well, can we go back, please. Can we focus in. Can we go back, please. Stop. Can we start again, please. I want to focus on the man on top of that APC. Stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, this is a shot of a blue APC. You see the man in the turret. He has a mask on. Can you see what he has in front of him, please?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can see, this is a Russian -- or a machine-gun, 7.62 millimetre, Russian fabrication.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go a little bit further, please. Stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So, we see a second blue APC. Can you tell what kinds of APCs these are?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can see, these are Hermelin tanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Are you able to see any kind of machine-gun on the Hermelin that is on the left side of this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where the commander is sitting, there seems to be a weapon; but whether it is a Kalashnikov or not, or an AK-47, or submachine-gun, I can't really see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go a little bit forward, please. Can we stop there, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, what is that on top of this APC?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is, once again, a 7.62 machine gun, Russian fabrication, on what appears to be mounted on a Hermelin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You used word "mounted," and the term "mount" and "mounts" and "mounted" came up several times during cross-examination. Take a look at this system of mounting, please. Is this the normal way that a machine-gun would be mounted on top of a APC?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. On these Hermelins, there is a device for German machine-guns of the type number 3, and this machine-gun is not compatible with the Russian type -- this device is not compatible with the Russian type. So they have adapted it to put the machine-gun on the opening hole for the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. So, when you say they have "adapted it," in other words, this is some kind of a makeshift mount?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is a makeshift way of putting the machine-gun on the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'd like to turn to another topic now, Mr. Hutsch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Before we do, simply for the record, Mr. Saxon has, I would suggest, given evidence to the effect that this video was from July and August of 2005. I will record for the record - or 2001, I apologise - for the record, that this particular video was shown to a witness in this particular case and that the witness in question was being asked whether he was able to date the incident or the events in question, and the witness has been unable to do so. As far as the Defence can say at this stage, there is no evidence on the record of the date of this particular video, or at least of the events to which it relates.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, when I spoke about July and August 2001, I was referring to the Prosecution's best knowledge as to when this -- this video-clip was made, Your Honour. There's no intention to provide evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber, in the end, will be concerned only with what is established by evidence, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go back to that last clip, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, when, if ever, did you see machine-guns like this mounted like this on APCs in Macedonia?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say, well, certainly to the end of 2001, and I would think in 2002 also.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When would you have first seen machine-guns like this mounted like this in 2001? Can you name, roughly, a month?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably in March or April, when the first Hermelins were delivered, so I think April, end of April, May, around that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to move on --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I see Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: I'm sorry to butt in again, Your Honour. Simply to clarify whether Mr. Saxon was asking about APCs or Hermelin of the police or of the army or both.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Point taken. I will clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Hutsch, when, if ever, did you see machine-guns like this mounted like this on APCs operated by the Macedonian police?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that period of time I just referred to, the end of April/beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to move on to a different topic now, Mr. Hutsch. I'd like to talk to you a little bit about the view that you had from your first observation point that was near the community of Radisani, where you were on the 10th of August, 2001, I believe, in the afternoon, and in the early morning of the 12th of August. On Monday, at page 6199 of the transcript, my colleague suggested to you that you could not see Ljuboten from Radisani because there is a hill in the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness what is Exhibit 2D73, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mettraux.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps, for the accuracy of the record, I believe this was in Radisani from the position from which Mr. Hutsch had claimed to make the observation which did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. I'm wondering if we can enlarge this. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just briefly, Mr. Hutsch, can you explain what you could see or what we can see from your first observation point? What are we looking at here, starting, perhaps, from the left moving towards the right?

utterances.speaker: FRANZ-JOSEF HUTSCH [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are looking at, on the left side, we're looking at the hill 631 that covers the western part of Ljuboten; and, on the right side, you can see the eastern part of Ljuboten with the mosque, and in the background is the mountain that you can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see my colleague on his feet again.

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
